- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to capture bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid bearish overcorrection.  
- Model consistently underestimates sharp upward moves (e.g., 70→80) — apply a 5–10% upward bias for such spikes.  
- Model overestimates downward moves (e.g., 80→70) — apply a 5–10% downward bias for such drops.  
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows persistent lag — model is 2–4 days behind true trend — adjust by adding 1–2 days of trend continuation in forecast.  
- After a sharp spike, model often overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2 price points above peak to avoid overcorrection.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% to align with reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum — add 1–2% upward bias for trending neutral periods.
